question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A walking school bus is a program in which adults lead a group of children on foot along a set route to school.
• Researchers at the Ressler Institute studied a walking school bus program in the town of Cobbleton over one school year.
• The researchers recorded each child's arrival time using the school's electronic attendance system.
• The enrolled children arrived late an average of 4 fewer times per term than they had before joining the program.
• All 212 enrolled children were in grades 1 through 3, and the study did not include older students.
• The researchers concluded that the walking school bus program reduces lateness among schoolchildren.

The student wants to present the study's conclusion while acknowledging a limitation of the study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: The researchers concluded that the walking school bus program reduces lateness among schoolchildren, although they recorded each child's arrival time using the school's electronic attendance system.
answer_b: The researchers concluded that the walking school bus program reduces lateness among schoolchildren, although all 212 children who enrolled were in grades 1 through 3.
answer_c: Children in grades 1 through 3 who joined the walking school bus program arrived late an average of 4 fewer times per term, although the study did not include older students.
answer_d: The walking school bus program reduces lateness among schoolchildren, as shown by the 212 children in grades 1 through 3 who arrived late an average of 4 fewer times per term.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it states the researchers' conclusion, that the walking school bus program reduces lateness among schoolchildren, and then acknowledges a real limitation of the study: all 212 enrolled children were in grades 1 through 3, so the study provides no evidence about older students. Attributing the conclusion to the researchers and flagging the narrow age range accomplishes both parts of the goal.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It presents the conclusion, but the "although" clause names a neutral procedural detail: how the researchers recorded arrival times. That detail does not weaken the conclusion or restrict whom it applies to, so it is not a limitation of the study.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It acknowledges a genuine limitation, that older students were not included, but it gives only the raw finding (4 fewer late arrivals per term) and never states the conclusion the researchers drew from it.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It states the conclusion as established fact for schoolchildren in general and mentions grades 1 through 3 only as the source of the evidence. It never acknowledges that the age range limits what the study shows, so it does not accomplish the goal of noting a limitation.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Haskett Marsh and Idlewick Marsh are two coastal wetlands that host ground-nesting shorebirds.
• Volunteers counted the nesting pairs at both marshes in 2019 and again in 2024.
• In 2019, Haskett Marsh had 40 nesting pairs, and Idlewick Marsh had 38.
• In 2024, Haskett Marsh had 160 nesting pairs, and Idlewick Marsh had 44.
• Between the two counts, Haskett Marsh installed fencing to keep foxes away from nests; Idlewick Marsh did not.

The student wants to emphasize how much greater the increase in nesting pairs was at Haskett Marsh than at Idlewick Marsh. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: From 2019 to 2024, the number of nesting pairs at Haskett Marsh rose from 40 to 160, and the number at Idlewick Marsh rose from 38 to 44.
answer_b: From 2019 to 2024, the number of nesting pairs at Haskett Marsh increased by more than the number of nesting pairs at Idlewick Marsh did.
answer_c: From 2019 to 2024, the number of nesting pairs rose by 120 at Haskett Marsh, twenty times the rise of 6 at Idlewick Marsh.
answer_d: In 2024, Haskett Marsh had 160 nesting pairs, more than three times the 44 nesting pairs counted at Idlewick Marsh.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it states the size of the difference between the two increases. The notes give counts, not increases, so the increases must be calculated: Haskett Marsh rose from 40 to 160 pairs, an increase of 120, and Idlewick Marsh rose from 38 to 44 pairs, an increase of 6. Because 120 is twenty times 6, the choice accurately emphasizes how much greater Haskett Marsh's increase was.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It accurately gives the starting and ending counts for each marsh, but it presents the figures separately and never compares the two increases, so it doesn't emphasize how much greater Haskett Marsh's increase was.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. It accurately says that Haskett Marsh's increase was larger, but it gives no sense of how much larger, so it doesn't emphasize the magnitude of the difference.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. The comparison is accurate (160 is more than three times 44), but it contrasts the 2024 totals rather than the increases from 2019 to 2024, and it understates how much greater Haskett Marsh's increase was.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Teodoro Vallespina is an architect who is widely known for the Cantera Cultural Center, a museum with a stepped concrete facade.
• The Cantera Cultural Center opened in 2004.
• Vallespina was born in 1951 and trained as an engineer before becoming an architect.
• Vallespina also designed the Danuyan Rain Market, a covered market in the town of Danuyan.
• The Rain Market was completed in 1998 and is far less famous than the Cantera Cultural Center.
• The Rain Market's roof is made of overlapping sheets of woven bamboo that channel rainwater into a cistern beneath the stalls.

The student wants to introduce a lesser-known work to an audience already familiar with its architect. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: Vallespina, who was born in 1951 and trained as an engineer before becoming an architect, designed the Danuyan Rain Market, a covered market with a roof of woven bamboo sheets.
answer_b: Vallespina is widely known for the Cantera Cultural Center, a museum that opened in 2004 and has a stepped concrete facade.
answer_c: Completed in 1998, a covered market in the town of Danuyan has a roof of overlapping woven bamboo sheets that channel rainwater into a cistern beneath the stalls.
answer_d: Far less famous than the Cantera Cultural Center, Vallespina's Danuyan Rain Market is a covered market with a woven bamboo roof that channels rainwater into a cistern below.
explanation: Choice D is the best answer because the audience already knows Vallespina, so the sentence can use the architect's name without explanation and spend its words on the lesser-known work. It names the work (the Danuyan Rain Market), identifies it as Vallespina's, says what it is (a covered market), and gives its distinctive feature (a woven bamboo roof that channels rainwater into a cistern). It also uses the notes' point that the market is far less famous than the Cantera Cultural Center, which fits the goal of presenting a lesser-known work.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It does name the market, credit Vallespina, and mention the bamboo roof, but it spends its opening clause on Vallespina's birth year and engineering training. This audience already knows Vallespina, so that biography does not help introduce the market, and the sentence never signals that the market is a lesser-known work, which the notes' comparison to the Cantera Cultural Center provides.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. It introduces the Cantera Cultural Center, the famous work this audience already knows, rather than the lesser-known Danuyan Rain Market the student wants to introduce. The Rain Market is never mentioned.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It describes the market's roof and drainage, but it never gives the work's name (the Danuyan Rain Market) or says that Vallespina designed it. Without those, the audience cannot connect the building to the architect they know, so the sentence does not introduce the work to them.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Many people assume that sunflowers keep turning their heads to follow the sun for their entire lives.
• Researchers at Tellwyn Agricultural College observed sunflowers over a full growing season.
• Young sunflowers in the study turned their heads from east to west during the day, following the sun.
• Mature sunflowers in the study, once their flower heads had fully opened, stopped turning and stayed facing east.
• The researchers also noted that a single sunflower head can contain more than 1,000 seeds.

The student wants to present a finding from the study as a challenge to a common assumption about sunflowers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: In the Tellwyn Agricultural College study, mature sunflowers with fully opened flower heads stopped turning and stayed facing east.
answer_b: Many people assume sunflowers follow the sun all their lives, yet in the Tellwyn study, mature sunflowers stopped turning and stayed facing east.
answer_c: Many people assume sunflowers follow the sun all their lives, yet in the Tellwyn study, young sunflowers turned their heads from east to west each day.
answer_d: Many people assume sunflowers follow the sun all their lives, yet the Tellwyn researchers noted that a single sunflower head can contain over 1,000 seeds.
explanation: Choice B is the best answer because it both states the common assumption (that sunflowers follow the sun all their lives) and presents the finding that contradicts it: in the Tellwyn study, mature sunflowers stopped turning and stayed facing east. It is the content of this finding, not just the word "yet," that runs against the assumption, so the sentence presents the finding as a challenge to the assumption.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It accurately reports the finding about mature sunflowers, but it never states the common assumption, so it does not present the finding as a challenge to that assumption. A reader of this sentence alone would not know what belief the finding is meant to call into question.
distractor_c_explanation: Choice C is incorrect. It states the assumption, but the finding it offers, that young sunflowers turned from east to west each day, is consistent with the assumption rather than contradicting it. The word "yet" makes the sentence sound like a challenge, but the evidence actually supports the assumption for young plants.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It states the assumption, but the detail it contrasts with it, that a single sunflower head can contain over 1,000 seeds, is accurate to the notes yet unrelated to whether sunflowers follow the sun. The seed count does not contradict anything the assumption claims.

question_text:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• In the 1800s, smelting iron ore required large amounts of coal to fuel furnaces.
• Brisford, a town in a hilly inland region, had no coal deposits within 60 kilometers.
• By 1870, Brisford was producing more iron than any other town in the region.
• Rich iron ore seams lay just beneath the hills around the town.
• In 1851, a canal opened between Brisford and the coal fields at Deepmere.
• Barges on the canal carried coal from Deepmere to Brisford's furnaces at a fraction of the cost of wagon transport.

The student wants to explain how Brisford's rise as the region's leading iron producer was possible despite a natural disadvantage. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
answer_a: Although Brisford had no coal deposits within 60 kilometers, it produced more iron than any other town in the region by 1870 because rich iron ore seams lay just beneath the hills around the town.
answer_b: By 1870, Brisford produced more iron than any other town in the region, a result of the canal opened in 1851, whose barges carried coal from Deepmere to the town's furnaces.
answer_c: Although Brisford had no coal deposits within 60 kilometers, it produced more iron than any other town in the region by 1870 because canal barges carried coal from Deepmere to its furnaces.
answer_d: Although Brisford had no coal deposits within 60 kilometers, the canal opened in 1851 carried coal from Deepmere to the town's furnaces by barge at a fraction of the cost of wagon transport.
explanation: Choice C is the best answer because it states the disadvantage (Brisford had no coal deposits within 60 kilometers), the outcome (by 1870 Brisford produced more iron than any other town in the region), and the factor that overcame the disadvantage (canal barges carried coal from Deepmere to the town's furnaces). Because smelting iron ore required large amounts of coal, the canal's coal supply explains how the outcome was possible despite the shortage.
distractor_a_explanation: Choice A is incorrect. It states the shortage of coal and the outcome, but the reason it gives, the iron ore seams near the town, does not address the shortage. Ore alone cannot fuel furnaces, so this explains why iron production was attractive but not how it was possible without nearby coal.
distractor_b_explanation: Choice B is incorrect. It gives the outcome and the canal that carried coal, but it never mentions that Brisford had no coal deposits within 60 kilometers. Without that disadvantage, the choice does not show how the rise was possible despite anything.
distractor_d_explanation: Choice D is incorrect. It states the disadvantage and describes how the canal delivered coal cheaply, but it never mentions that Brisford became the region's leading iron producer. It therefore does not explain how that rise was possible.
